Cause: fork PR #25284 (`mig-builds/objectstack`, opened 2026-10-22T19:52Z) also declares `Fixes #25282` and edits the same two files. This PR's diff cannot clear it. **Escalated to the seat** (fork-PR handling per `references/external-contributions.md`).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ca74ad754d0c79c1376ddc15cfc5f102c24745dc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/flow-value-slot-template.ts + packages/spec/src/automation/flow-value-slot-template.test.ts, packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts (`rewriteIndexedHas`, `indexedHasSelection`), packages/formula/src/cel-has-indexed-receiver.test.ts (controls), packages/spec/src/automation/flow-template-token.ts (`celPath`, `CEL_KEYWORDS`, `celHeadReadsThroughVars`), packages/spec/package.json (`files[]`), .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml (`changeset-check`)

Read at 2026-10-23T07:08Z: card #25282 body (now carrying ruling 6358845679) and all three comments (claim 6356807456, os-dev-report 6357243074, ruling 6358845679), PR #25367 body, file list and both comments (docs-drift 6357242841, the earlier record 6357326028 on `d3abc1c8`), the net diff `origin/main...ca74ad75` (merge-base `c109bfc1`; 2 files, +7/−5), the 49 check-runs on `ca74ad75`, and fork PR #25284's state. The earlier record was read as an input and re-judged, not adopted.

Head provenance: `ca74ad75` is a merge of `origin/main` (`c109bfc1`) into the dev commit `d3abc1c8`. The two files in scope are byte-identical between `d3abc1c8` and `ca74ad75` (`git diff` empty over them), and no commit on `main` between the merge-base and today's tip touches them or the cited `cel-engine.ts` / `flow-template-token.ts`. The merge is a real merge (133 files from `main`), not an empty commit.

### ① Derived judgments

- **No accept set and no public surface moves — right.** The diff is the `guardOf` JSDoc (flow-value-slot-template.ts:317–324) and one `it(...)` title (test:201). `guardOf`'s predicate `segments[0].startsWith('$') || /^\d+$/ || CEL_KEYWORDS.has(s)` and its emitted `has(vars.a) && has(vars.a.b) ? vars.a.b : null` chain are untouched; `guardOf` is module-private (no `export`); every assertion in the test is unchanged.
- **"`has()` refuses an index as the last step of its argument … an index before the last step is a presence test" — right, read in the code PR #25275 landed.** `indexedHasSelection` (cel-engine.ts:1557–1569) lowers a `has()` only when its argument is a `.` selection whose root is not a bare identifier; an argument that is itself an index node (`a[0]`, `vars["$x"]`, `record["in"]`) is not a `.` selection and is left to cel-js's macro, which faults `has() invalid argument`. The docblock on `rewriteIndexedHas` (:1498–1502) states the same rule. Controls pin both arms: `cel-has-indexed-receiver.test.ts:93–101` (`has(record.items[0])` refused at compile, validate and evaluate) and `:106–112` (`has(a[0].b.c)` → `a[0].b.?c.hasValue()`; `has(a[0])` untouched, hence refused).
- **"a numeric segment, a `$`-named head or a keyword segment is read by index, so one of its tests would end on that index" — right.** `celPath` (flow-template-token.ts:191–200) writes a numeric segment as `[n]`, a keyword segment (`CEL_KEYWORDS` = `true|false|null|in`, :113) as `["kw"]`, and a `$`-named head as `vars["$x"]` via `celHeadReadsThroughVars` (CEL has no identifier spelling for `$`). A step-at-a-time guard matching that spelling would at some step be `has(vars.rows[0])`, `has(vars["$x"])` or `has(vars.record["in"])`, each refused. The PR body's measured table (`has(vars.rows) && has(vars.rows[0]) && has(vars.rows[0].name)` refused) agrees with the code reading. Nit carried from the earlier record, not blocking: `guardOf` never calls `celPath`; the docblock implies rather than states that the hypothetical guard would borrow `celPath`'s spelling.
- **The non-mechanism part of the old prose was already right and is kept — right.** The card itself says only the reason was stale; the "gets no guard" outcome and the second paragraph (`Unknown variable` / `No such key` / `&&` short-circuit) are unchanged.
- **Test title — right.** The new title states the same rule as the docblock; the two assertions on `{rows.0.name}` (`source: 'rows[0].name'` present, "the guarded form" absent) are unchanged, so nothing is re-pinned or loosened. No other "index anywhere" / "names alone" prose remains in either file (grep at head: the two remaining `anywhere` hits, :29 and :946, are unrelated sentences).
- **Card ask met in full:** two prose edits, no behaviour change, landed after #25275 (merged 2026-10-22T20:41Z).

### ② Semver level

- **`skip-changeset` — right.** `@objectstack/spec` `files[]` ships `dist`, `src/**/*.zod.ts` and metadata, not this `.ts`; `guardOf` is unexported and a plain JSDoc on a private function is dropped from `dist`. The PR body's dist probe (old sentence 0 hits, `ABSENT_SENTENCE` positive control present) is consistent with that reading. `Check Changeset` on this head reads `skipped` (both runs), which is the workflow's own `skip-changeset`-label exemption (pr-automation.yml:244–247), not a red.
- **`Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` — right.** Plain `no`, not `no (narrowing)`: nothing is removed or narrowed; the PR publishes nothing.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Branch `claude/project-thread-tfi1b0`** (platform lets the card thread push only its thread branch; recorded in claim 6356807456) — accepted. `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`: success.
- **Duplicate claim, the sole FAIL cause on `d3abc1c8` — resolved.** Ruling 6358845679 (letter A, maintainer 「同意」 2026-10-23T06:22Z): land #25367, credit and close #25284. Fork PR #25284 is `closed`, not merged, at 2026-10-23T06:24:05Z. `No other open PR may claim the same issue`: success on this head (both runs). `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`: success.
- **Ruling step 2 said "relay re-run, ⛔ no empty commit"; what happened is a merge of `origin/main` into the branch.** That is a new head rather than a re-run of the old one, but it is not an empty commit (133 files from `main`), the two files in scope are byte-identical to `d3abc1c8`, and `main` did not touch any cited file. Accepted as a deviation of route, not of substance; noted so the seat's report can own it.
- **Ruling step 3 (landing commit carries the `Co-authored-by` trailer with the contributor's noreply email) is owed by the lander, not by this diff.** The PR body carries a `Co-authored-by: mig-builds (fork PR #25284, …)` line WITHOUT the email in the name-plus-address form GitHub recognises, so a squash message taken from the body would not attribute the co-author. Escalated to `domain:spec` seat 1: put the full trailer, exactly as the ruling spells it, in the landing commit message.
- **Check-runs on the head: 49 total, 38 `success`, 11 `skipped`, 0 `failure`, 0 `in_progress`.** Every gate family the earlier record found unfinished (`Build Core`, `Test Core` 1/6–6/6, Type Check, Lint) has concluded `success`; `Spec property liveness`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Documentation Links`: success. Docs-drift 6357242841 reports the changed file yields no anchor — a coverage note, not a finding, and no docs page restates the `has()` mechanism this docblock states (the card names the two stale spots and the diff fixes exactly those).
- **`open_questions: []`, `deviations: none`** in the os-dev-report — nothing to answer. `NOT MEASURED: check:dual-build-cjs-loads` was left to CI; the CI families that cover it are green on this head.
